sections.title: Build a mask
sections.summary: Trace one part of the idea.

blocks.caption: Bit syntax is compact in every language, so names and parentheses keep the intent readable.

java.code:
int mask = 1 << bit;
boolean isOn = (n & mask) != 0;

javascript.code:
const mask = 1 << bit;
const isOn = (n & mask) !== 0;

cpp.code:
int mask = 1 << bit;
bool isOn = (n & mask) != 0;

blocks.prompt: What should a bit trace check first?
choices: The state that proves the next move
The final button the user clicks
The color of the code editor
blocks.why: Check the mask before the final boolean or number. The mask says which binary position is being tested.

blocks.prompt: Which debugging habit fits bit manipulation best?
choices: Trace one small state change before trying a larger input
Start with the largest hidden case
Change the data structure after each failed test
Ignore the saved state and read only the final answer
blocks.why: Small numbers make each bit visible. Once the mask is correct, the same operation scales to larger integers.

sections.title: Common bit mistakes
sections.summary: Bit code often confuses decimal digits with binary positions. The value 10 is not bit position ten.
